# Mr.Latin

> Zero-config, zero-dependency, drop-in library that translates any web page into
> any language with a natural, conversational tone. Language only — adaptive
> theming is the sibling library, TheSwitch.

## What it does
Reads the visible text already on the page, translates it in place (RTL-aware),
and keeps dynamically-added content translated via a MutationObserver. No string
extraction, no JSON catalogs, no build step. The text on screen IS the source.

## Install / use
- npm: `npm install mr.latin` then `import { MrLatin } from "mr.latin"; await new MrLatin().start();`
- CDN (no build): `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mr.latin/dist/mr-latin.global.js" data-mr-latin data-languages="en,de,fr,ar"></script>`

## Two tiers
- Tier 1 (default, zero-config): on-device Chromium Translator API — free, private, no key, no setup.
- Tier 2 (opt-in): set `endpoint` / `data-endpoint` to your own LLM proxy for conversational *transcreation* (Claude recommended). The key stays on your server.

## Core API
- `new MrLatin(options).start(): Promise<MrLatin>`
- methods: `setLanguage(code)`, `refresh()`, `destroy()`, `subscribe(fn) => unsubscribe`
- props: `language`, `busy`
- options: `sourceLanguage`, `language`, `languages`, `providers`, `dictionary`, `glossary`, `tone`, `register`, `autoTranslate`, `persist`, `widget`, `skipSelectors`, `endpoint`, `onSuggest`
- providers: `BrowserTranslationProvider`, `createLLMProvider`, `createHttpProvider`, `createLibreTranslateProvider`
- helpers: `nativeLanguageName`, `isRTL`, `applyDirection`, `formatNumber`, `formatCurrency`, `formatDate`, `flagFor`, `buildTranscreationPrompt`

## Notes for AI agents integrating this
- `tone` (conversational|warm|playful|neutral|formal) and `register` (casual|neutral|formal) drive transcreation so output matches the *situation* (a heading vs a button vs body copy vs legal fine print).
- Exact overrides via `dictionary[targetLang][sourceText]` always win; the cache key is (text, target, tone, register).
- Exclude content with `translate="no"`, `class="notranslate"`, or `data-mr-latin-skip`.
- It is framework-agnostic; React/Vue/Svelte adapters exist at `mr.latin/react|vue|svelte`.
